runConfig.positivePrompt: Scientific educational image-to-video for ages five to fourteen. Static locked wide camera, one continuous forward-only five-second shot with no cuts. Preserve the attached approved still as the exact first-frame Iguanodon bernissartensis identity, robust quadrupedal anatomy, left-facing full-body composition, lighting, palette, skin markings, woodland, ground, and crop reference. Exactly one complete Iguanodon remains with one beaked skull, two forelimbs with the same conical thumb spikes and weight-bearing central digits, two hind limbs, four planted feet total, and one complete long tail. After a brief hold, the dinosaur itself makes one calm browsing motion: the complete skull, connected muscular neck, throat, shoulder base, and upper chest lower together by seven to nine degrees and move forward by about two percent of frame width toward the low vegetation. The beak stays closed and the final second holds the new lowered pose. Preserve the eye, cheek, beak proportions, neck thickness, hands, thumb spikes, all four feet, every readable digit, pelvis, and tail. Keep the background and plants still; the dinosaur moves toward them without plant animation. No return, reverse, second dip, bite cycle, step, walk, body turn, or loop.
